utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes. We were -- we are supposed to deal with the associated exhibits, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Before we do that, if I could just raise one issue with respect to the timing. First of all, Dr. Karadzic would like to ask that the Chamber give him additional time for the cross-examination of this witness given the length of the direct examination and also a number of documents we wish to put to the witness in aid of our own case. In addition, I understand that the Prosecution would like to determine at the outset of today's session whether or not it's necessary for the next witness to be waiting during the day today for the possibility that he might testify, and I'll let Mr. Tieger address that with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Only this, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. I understood from Mr. Robinson that the Defence would be raising this motion so I wanted to bring to the Court's attention any facts -- scheduling factors that might be relevant to the Court one way or another, and there are two. One is the fact that we have spoken to the Defence and both agreed that in light of certain scheduling issues that Mr. Erdemovic should be heard first thing on Monday. Now, that's of course up to the Court, but both parties feel that that would be appropriate under the circumstances. That would mean that if Mr. Milovanovic started, he would only be on the stand at best for a very brief time before another witness would be interposed, which is a factor the Court may want to consider does not seem all that desirable. And the other factor that Mr. Robinson alluded to is that if at all possible, we would not want to bring Mr. Milovanovic here unnecessarily to wait around, so we would, if at all possible, ask the Court for a decision one way or another at least before the lunch recess so that we -- and as early as possible so that we avoid having Mr. Milovanovic come and sit around for no reason. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. That's helpful. Mr. Robinson, Mr. Karadzic had about 20 minutes yesterday and will have about -- a bit less than four and a half hours today. If he had all today, would it not be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll make an effort, Your Excellency, to complete my cross-examination today if I have the whole day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has been our Chamber's practice, has it not, that if the accused is sticking to the relevant questions and at the end of the allotted session there still remains some relevant factors, the Chamber has been allowing the accused to put questions as much as possible. So I would like the accused to focus on relevant matters and prioritise his questioning. But we'll deal with the associated exhibits first. So all the -- except for all those that have already been admitted will be admitted, but I wanted -- I told you, Ms. Edgerton, that to deal with a couple of exhibits if you want to tender them.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Oh, pardon me, Your Honours. The only one I'd like, with Your Honours' permission, to deal with is 65 ter number 01917 as the other exhibit you referred to yesterday is something that falls within the material that is been redacted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- from the 92 ter evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. You follow everything, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. President, but just so that the Registry knows not to admit as associated exhibits those that fall within the redacted portion of the transfer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have 65 ter number 01917 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: General, 65 ter 01917 is another operations report dated 13 July 1995 from the VRS Main Staff to the president like those that you reviewed yesterday. I'd like you first in respect of this document to have a look at the number that appears above the dateline. Does that number 03/3-194 denote anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the number of the organ where this document was produced. It's the operations and training administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that's the administration that you served with?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go over to the signature block on the last page, please. Now, here as with the reports you looked at -- a number of the reports you looked at yesterday, we see some initials above the signature block of General Miletic on the last page, "nt/gp." Do you know whose initials those are?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedeljko Trkulja, and I don't know the person who typed this out.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And could we please go over to page 3, paragraph 6 in both English and B/C/S under the heading which relates to matters in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see, General, about halfway through paragraph 6, the line which reads: "The enemy from the former enclave of Srebrenica is in a state of total disarray and the troops are surrendering in large numbers to the VRS"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, given the process for preparation of these reports that you described yesterday, is this information or does this reflect information which would have been contained in the operations report from the Drina Corps command to the VRS Main Staff, this same date?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could that be a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Same objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, we don't object to this, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4464, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further from me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Registrar approach the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Then back to you, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Excellencies. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we were talking about reports and my question is, in the Tolimir case at page 11971, you said the following: You said that frequently subordinate commanders would sometimes intentionally fail to portray the situation accurately. For example, if they'd lost a zone or if there was an action that they didn't take. Sometimes this was intentional. Sometimes it was accidental. Do you stand by that testimony today, and do you agree that there are few who would have provided information on their failures in the hope that they would correct their failures by the time the next report was due?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Such things did occur.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at the Croatian intercepts. I think it's a 65 ter document 035 -- 35042. Page 234. Could it be enlarged, please, in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, could you please read through the Serbian version. No, the Serbian text isn't the right one. 234. Yes, now we have it. General, in spite of all our protective measures, the Croats recorded every word we said, so please have a look at this intercept of my conversation with the colonel at the time and later General Tomanic. It's dated the 11th of August, 1992. Could you please read it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11th of August, 1992, 0720 hours, 18562, Bosnia and Herzegovina. "We learned the following from the conversation between Karadzic Tomanic which was conducted at 003 [as interpreted] hours. We --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, did you mean to ask him to read it aloud?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I saw that we have the translation, he doesn't have to read it out aloud. He can just read -- read it to himself and tell us what he knows about this and what he thinks about this. Then I'll put my question to him. He doesn't have to read it out aloud provided that the translation is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, General Obradovic, when you're done with your reading, could you let us know so that Mr. Karadzic can put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that General Obradovic might start suffering from seasickness given the way the text is being moved around.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think, from reading the intercept, that the date of the intercept is actually incorrect, the year, that is. I think this is an intercept from 1993, 11 August 1993, rather than 11 August 1992. I say that purely on the basis of the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that that is the case, because the crisis concerns Igman and Bjelasnica, those areas, and that was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So have you read this intercept, General? Yes, Mr. Karadzic, what is your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Please, neglect or ignore the swear words I used in anger, only related to the soldiers, I believe, but do you agree that this corresponds to what you were saying in the case of General Tolimir? You were saying that these reports might not be complete, that they weren't always helpful, and that there were reasons for me to be dissatisfied.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The contents of this intercept does prove that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, do you agree that especially the first year or the first two years of war, I had too much trust in foreigners and sometimes I wasn't fair towards our generals and took what foreign people told me to be true, whereas that was not always correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this page be admitted into evidence. MFI, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Edgerton, do you have any observation? Did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I suspect there maybe a practice in place that I haven't followed because I haven't appeared before Your Honours lately, but I was just querying why this should be marked for identification when Dr. Karadzic confirmed the date and is one of the participants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he testify? So we'll deal with it at one go later on. Let us mark it for identification as a D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2091, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I hope that the other participants will also forgive me for the vocabulary I used, but that is a male and military vocabulary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, in the Popovic case you also described an event when you saw that something had been incorrectly portrayed. It has to do with your meeting with the Lieutenant Djordjevic. Could you repeat that for our benefit? You saw, as did others, that reports were not always accurate because people would omit to report on matters that might have an unfavourable effect on them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that, in that case, there was a discussion on the value of reports and the document from the Chief of Staff in which he warned units about the quality of reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but for the benefit of the participants, I would like to say that it's in the Popovic case, and the pages are 28275 and 28276.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned an example, because up until the 1st of September, 1994, I was in Posavina and to the south, in the area of Teslic, on the slopes of Vlasic, and in that area that lieutenant, not Djordjevic but Boro Djurdjevic, he went to Crna Rijeka. He met me. I asked him, What's going on in your area? And he then said that Djukici and Panici had fallen. He mentioned other names of Serbian villages to the south of Blatnica. He said, Everything's gone. And I said, Don't fabricate these things, I've read a report from the 1st Krajina Corps last night. He stood by his claims. I conveyed this information to General Miletic. And some time later the Chief of Staff called me. General Miletic was with him already. I realised that he had told him what I had told him. He called Tolimir and asked him to check this. In front of us he called the chief of security of the 1st Krajina Corps, Colonel Stevo Bogojevic, and asked him whether it was correct that those villages and that that area had fallen into Muslim hands. He said yes, and General Tolimir then told him to write a report for him. He said, Well, I can't because of the boss, and his boss was the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps. That's what I said in the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember an incident when there was some sort of a parade of our soldiers and they were within the range of their multiple-rocket launchers, and one of their rockets killed 11 of our soldiers somewhere near Donji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the light brigade had lined up the troops for some sort of a ceremony, and the area where he had them lined up was within the range of the mortars or of the artillery, and they were then targeted by the artillery and sustained these losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that we did not lodge a protest because it was legitimate?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of us having protested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, do you remember that I received a report on this in 11 days' time. Every day they informed me of one person who had killed [as interpreted]. If they had informed me in one day, I would have had to launch an investigation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. At the time I wasn't in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But as far as you know, Ms. Edgerton asked you about reports sent to the Main Staff and asked you how the essence of the reports was conveyed by using the same words in reports sent to me. Do you agree that reports from -- or there are brigade reports sent to corps. In the corps you just have the essence which is then conveyed to the Main Staff. In the Main Staff, they also abbreviate these reports and send the essence of the reports to me and to other addresses, to the government, to the ministry and so on.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this isn't from the brigade. The brigades receive reports from their subordinated units. They then edit them and send them as a single report from that brigade to the corps command. In the corps command, all the reports from brigades, regiments and independent battalions are put into a more succinct form and sent to the Main Staff. And in the Main Staff, on the basis of all the reports received from the corps, from the aircraft unit, the anti-aircraft unit, the HQ support units and so on and so forth, we then send a report to the president and to all the addresses referred to in the reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic. A couple of matters, Mr. Tieger and Ms. Edgerton. I wonder if I was clear enough that Mr. Milovanovic does not need to be brought in today. And second thing, one of the associated exhibits is an intercept. I forgot to say that that will be marked for identification as well. Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that if every piece of paper were to reach me which had to do with reports of that day, it would be quite a sizable pile, up to 1.000 pages, taking into account all the information, whereas the two or three pages I received from the Main Staff basically contained the gist of all the pages produced from the level of companies up to brigades and so on. In your assessment, how many pages would that be for the entire army?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be an enormous amount. If we bear in mind that each corps had 10 brigades on average times the number of pages needed for their reports, it would be an enormous number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then say that this pyramid has its base in the lowest-ranking units and the peak is in the Main Staff. And the president, who received even less material than the Main Staff, the president only received two or three pages of the summaries of all the reporting that had been done.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 11, I said "taking into account all the formations of our army" and not "all information." Thank you. Could we next see P3035. Perhaps this was not announced, but we realise there was a need for us to show it. In any case, it is a P exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, General, that the date is the 15th of June. It is a decision on the formation, organisation, as well command and control of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is dated the 15th of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that as of that date the armed forces were official in terms of their existence?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the decision which established the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the document itself. When you're done with the first page, do tell us so that we can move on to the next.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go straight to item 6. I believe it will be enough for the General to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the commander of the Main Staff is hereby authorised to determine close organisation and establishment of units depending on conditions and circumstances?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what item 6 of this decision says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back to item 4 which was on the first page -- no. Sorry. Can we agree that this is my signature and stamp from the period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have item 4 on the other page. I don't know where it is in English though. Please look at item 4.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: If the accused is going to read, please wait for the English translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The control and command of operative groups in the front shall be performed by the Main Staff of the Army of the SR of Bosnia and Herzegovina which shall be directly subordinated to the president [as interpreted] of the SR of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the Presidency of the SR of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a collective presidential body retained only the strategic level of command within its remit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the conclusion of this provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, are you familiar with any single case in which the Main Staff received some information about crimes and that it was kept by the Main Staff without it being forwarded to the president or, later on, Presidency?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am reading the interpretation of my question. Would the Main Staff keep anything secret if they received such information from the field? In other words, if they received such information, they would report on it; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it possible, in keeping with what you have said so far, that someone from the field could avoid communicating information about his or her mistake to a higher level?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is such a possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General Obradovic, you may help us, the Chamber, in this regard. You confirmed that the Presidency retained only the strategic level of command within its remit. What does it mean in concrete terms? What other levels of command were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is the strategic, operational, and tactical level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you explain the difference of those levels.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The corps are at the operational level. They make operational decisions, whereas brigades and lower-ranking units are at the tactical level. The strategic level is at the state level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Or to be even more accurate, General, do we agree that the state, for example, decides on its strategic position to defend this or that or to achieve this or that, whereas all operational and tactical matters are in the hands of the military profession?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All operational and tactical activities are joined ultimately in a strategic project or collection of plans which need to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We need to go back to 1992. When the war broke out, you were in Derventa; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There you commanded a garrison, or were you a member of the garrison command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade command where I was was part of the garrison brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that at the time in Derventa, you as the JNA had a very difficult time even before the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina broke out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I frequently referred to that period just before the war as being more difficult than the war itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we say that it was because your hands were tied and because you were caught in a crossfire, so to speak, between the Serb territorial forces and the Croatian Army which was present there? Can you describe briefly the situation for us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last or third stage of the Jedinstvo plan envisaged that the units of the 17th Corps, which was headquartered in Tuzla and included the area south of the Sava River, including mine -- my brigade, be that all such units be made part of the R classification. The -- my command was also the garrison command, which means that it dealt with general logistical matters for the 18th Partisan Brigade and its command, which was also part of the R classification group. We also took care of the mixed anti-armour brigade, which was a front line unit or a combat unit. In other words, we did not have many soldiers at our disposal, whereas we had to secure all depots of supplies, ammunition, and other war assets. At the time, the political leadership of the HDZ and the SDA, based on certain requests from the Republic of Croatia, tried to exert influence over members of their ethnic communities in order for them not to respond to any draft calls to the units of the JNA. Running in parallel, there were more and more occurrences of Croats, Serbs, and Muslims arming themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Could we have 1D5131. It is your document to the Secretariat for National Defence. While we are waiting for it, General, do we agree that the municipal national defence secretaries were bodies or organs of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence in municipalities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this document of yours from 1991? It is in early 1991. The Yugoslav Presidency was concerned over different formations and demanded that they be controlled. Can you tell us what is the gist of the document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the gist is that there were concerns that TO weapons would be taken as it was a component of the armed forces comprising the JNA and the TO. The TO was under the remit of the republican defence organs, and in a way the TO was a people's army. Wherever in any given municipality there were political leaders and a majority of the population belonging to a single ethnic group, they tried to take such assets for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So already in April 1991, there was a need to order the disbanding of all units which were not part of the regular armed forces.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2092, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, you were aware, were you not, that such illegal paramilitary formations were being formed, especially the Patriotic League and the Green Berets? You discussed the issue of the Patriotic League in General Tolimir's trial, which is 65 ter 23610, on page 129.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 35042, page 24.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we enlarge the image for the General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read this? We see your name as well. On the 4th of April, 1992, it seems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. English page shows the previous document that we saw earlier on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need this page, page 24, I believe. The date is the 4th of April. There seems to be no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that we see here there were already problems in certain municipalities and barricades in places such as Kulina and elsewhere? Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So there is no English translation for this. Then collapse, yes, the English page. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what happened on the 4th of April when these problems occurred? The barricades were set up by the HDZ government, and they prevented you from functioning normally. There was also mortar fire on the Vuk Karadzic Street. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The date here is the 4th of April, 1300 hours. Colonel Stublincevic was the Chief of Staff of the 17th Corps and he was also the deputy. General Janko Sava's deputy. Here he is speaking to Captain First Class Nedeljko Stajcic because I was absent and he was replacing me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have a look at page 19. On the 23rd of March, 1992, Ms. Plavsic and Mr. Abdic were in Bosanski Brod because there was a crisis there too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please remember these page numbers because I will later request that they be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 23rd of March is the date.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 27th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we can look at this too. Do you remember the massacre in the Sijekovac village?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And on that occasion, the republican leadership went with Franjo Boras, Dr. Biljana Plavsic, and Fikret Abdic. There was another man with them whose surname was Isak. I don't know what his position was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this page also be remembered. We'll be tendering it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, I have difficulty understanding the relevance of these lines of questions. Why -- in particular why Mr. Karadzic needed intercepts to put these questions while complaining about the shortage of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think he's best placed to answer that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic, we'll mark them for identification, but I urge you to concentrate on more -- more the critical, the important issues to the case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I fully agree with you, but I want to establish the context for my next questions about our relationship with the Muslims and Croats regardless of what was happening to us. I'll skip a lot of questions. Could we see page 67 of this very same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Before or while we're waiting for that to come up, I wonder if Dr. Karadzic can help us out a little bit. He referred the General to page 129 of the General's Tolimir testimony saying that he had discussed the issue of the Patriotic League there, and I've got page 129 from e-court in front of me and it's a recounting of a farewell party for General Zivanovic on the 20th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So maybe we could just find out what he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But all that was referred to was Patriotic League, so I just let it go. But be precise in giving the reference, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, I couldn't have been more precise. 12, 12, 9. Twelve a hundred and twenty-nine. After 1200 onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably it was interpretation, but let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the presence of the 108th Brigade from the Croatian Army mentioned here on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at page 32. It's probably 32. Something seems to have got a bit confused. Do you remember Cardak? What is Cardak?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 80, please. Page 80.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cardak is a settlement within the Derventa area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us here who the Black Shirts, and what is being announced here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some Croatian Army units had black uniforms, and the people would therefore call them the Black Shirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with these Black Shirts, and from which war, which units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the Second World War. The Jure Francetic Legion from Bosnia-Herzegovina was well known.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we read this out.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 24th of April, 1992, 21769, from a conversation of the Black Shirts we have discovered that this evening they will carry out a massacre in the Cardak settlement in the Derventa area. This is what Junak said." Junak must be a code-name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we see page 83, please. Can you find your name here where it says that Colonel -- Lieutenant-Colonel Obradovic wasn't familiar with Cardak. No. 83 is still about Cardak. And the event that already happened is being described here. Isn't that correct? Had that massacre already taken place in Cardak as the Croatian Secret Service said on the basis of intercepted conversations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So does that show that they did not inform General Bobetko about the matter and the massacre wasn't prevented?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as they had information in advance, they didn't prevent this. I don't know whether it's a matter of not reporting or someone's intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we see page 85, please. This is the last one from this series. The 27th of April. Can you see your name, your surname here somewhere?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says that you were praised here. He was fighting to get the people out of the village, and it says Obradovic wasn't familiar with the situation. So we have to praise the man who was fighting to get them out. So you directly saw that this massacre was perpetrated.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the pages that we have just looked at admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber was concerned about the frequent usage of untranslated documents, Mr. Karadzic, in addition to the concerns that I expressed as to the relevance, but we'll mark them for identification. We dealt with six pages in total. Page 24, 19, 64 -- 67, 80, 83, 85? Sixty-seven was not used. So we'll mark those five pages for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is 85, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, 85.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2092, and a new 65 ter will be assigned to this, and that will be 65 ter number 35042C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Registrar approach the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will get to the point. Very quickly, General, do you agree that these crimes were perpetrated by paramilitary formations of Bosnian-Herzegovinian Muslims and Croats and the regular Croatian Army, the 108th Brigade, the Zenga, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in spite of this, General, is it correct that in your area of responsibility there were several Muslim villages and settlements that had remained peaceful and some even remained loyal to Yugoslavia and the republic -- and Republika Srpska, and they participated as members in the army and no one ever touched them? Is it correct that in your municipality of Bosanski Dubocac -- well, that municipality was on good terms with us, Bosanski Kobas as well, and there are some other villages which were on good terms with us? Could you briefly and rapidly tell us what the situation looked like?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Dubocac it was divided. It was both a Muslim and Croat village, but they were divided, the Muslims and Croats. Some of them were in the HVO and others were in our army. The Omeragic village, Turski Luzani, Turski Kalenderovci, these places were compact. They were there throughout the war. And the unit that was with Croats and with their men was called Mesa Selimovic. Its first commander was a reserve major. His name was Ismet Dzuheric, and after Ismet Dzuheric, since he went to Bosnian -- Bosanski Brod for work obligation purposes, well, he was attacked in Sijekovac, in fact, when this attack was launched on Sijekovac. It's the Brod municipality. Later it was the Reserve Major Nusret Dizdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me assist the Chamber to understand this, because on the basis of the names it won't be possible. Is it true that the names of the villages you've mentioned are Muslim villages and these commanders were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this gentleman Ismet Djukovic is now the president of the Brod municipality in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's involved in politics. I think he's a socialist. He's not the president of the municipality. He's the president of the Municipal Assembly in the Brod municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that Mesa Salipovic [as interpreted] is a great Serbian writer who comes from a Muslim family?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He declared himself to be a Serbian writer. Ivo Andric is declared to be a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You'd say a Catholic not a Croat, in fact; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that we -- that the Serbs initially fled from Derventa, they were driven out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the presence of the Croatian Army, the HVO, and all other paramilitary units, the Serbian population on the whole left Derventa when the Republika Srpska Army was established after the JNA left on the 19th of May, when we consolidated and organised ourselves, and when because of the blockade we had to open up a life-saving road on the ground because we couldn't provide oxygen for the maternity ward in Banja Luka via air, and as a result 12 babies died. Since that was the situation, the 1st Krajina Corps planned an operation called Corridor and we opened up a land corridor which reached as far as Bijeljina. We did this by engaging our forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And within that context, Derventa was liberated; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just put a pause between question and answer. Bear in mind that this is also translated into French. Now you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Within that operation was Derventa liberated? And is it correct that after we entered Derventa, the Muslims remained in town? They went on living there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We entered Derventa and liberated it on the 4th of July, 1992. The Muslims remained with us. They continued to live there, as did a number of Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, did you ever hear an order or intention or a wish to the effect that there should be no Muslims and Croats in Republika Srpska and that they should be expelled?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for telling us about 1992. I wanted you to tell us about it because you were there on the spot. Let us now go back to the question of reports. I would like to put something to you, reports to the president in July 1995. We reviewed about 162 reports from that period of time, and we chose 23 that the Main Staff sent to the president of the republic at this critical point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we now call up 65 ter 3848. One hundred sixty-two until the end of my term of office, and in July there were 23 of them, from the 1st of July onwards. So can we have a look at this. Can we please have paragraph 6 in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We agree that this is the 3rd of July; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6, please. Please focus on paragraph 6. Does it say here that in the part of the front line facing the enclaves, the enemy used PN and the situation in the Drina Corps is as follows --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could we please have an accurate reference. We cannot find this in the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do we see the paragraph you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is paragraph 6. It has to do with DK. That's the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is (b).

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English it also moves on to the next page. Well, yes. You can see part of it. Subparagraph (b), visible targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it clear here, General, sir, that these were the objectives from where fire was opened at us? Therefore, are these military objectives?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the president conclude on the basis of this that we have some offensive intentions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except for the activity that is based on the words that there should be an appropriate response.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2094, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 65 ter 4019. Can we have a look at that. That's the report on the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We do agree that this is the 4th of July, 1995; right? The president of the republic, all corps. This is the usual kind of report; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Once again can we have paragraph 6 that has to do with the Drina Corps. Please take a look at it. It is subparagraph (a), and there is a reference to the enemy, and it says that there were no hostile activities, and (b) says that the corps units are at a level of combat readiness that was ordered. They are firmly holding on to the lines reached, regrouping their forces in order to completely close off the Srebrenica enclave. General, sir, would you say that the question of defence positions, is this military language that is purely defensive?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, General, sir, that this is something that the president of the republic could have known because that is what the report said, that was the way in which the report was written and in no other way; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be admitted as the next Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D2095, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have a look at 65 ter 4111.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that this is also a regular daily report from the 5th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to paragraph 6 yet again. It always has to do with the Drina Corps. In English it is page 3. Subparagraph (a), it says that the enemy carried out intermittent combat operations concentrating on the part of the front line that is facing the enclaves, and from time to time intensified reconnaissance activities, intermittently firing PAMs on our positions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And as for our corps, it says that they are highly vigilant, that they are carrying out engineering works at positions and setting up barricades. Again, this is defensive activity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, engineering works at positions and setting up barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, if somebody is carrying out engineering works at positions, is it not correct that then there is no intention to advance, rather, the intention is to stay there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Engineering works at positions means that optimal conditions are created for activity and defence protection at that line that had been reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? Has it been admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think so. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2096, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have a look at 65 ter 16542. I'm sorry, 3853.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that this is also the usual kind of comprehensive daily report at the end of the day, the 6th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have paragraph 6 again. Could you please focus on paragraph 6. It's the last sentence of subparagraph (a), it says: "In the Srebrenica enclave, it was noted that the enemy was grouping and occasionally firing from infantry weapons on the units of our units of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade." And then there is also a reference further on that the forces had been prepared and grouped for active combat operations towards the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. Do we agree, General, that it's only on the 6th that the corps decides to respond more actively to these provocations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Grouping and preparation for activity vis-a-vis the enclave is referred to here specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit D2097.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although you were on sick leave, General, were you informed that because of the Muslim offensive against Sarajevo, the 28th Division was active in the area of Srebrenica in order to drag out our forces and to keep the Drina Corps active in the enclave? I mean, so that the Drina Corps could not help the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is customary in all armies, in order to mask one's true intentions, what is done in particular areas where there are no serious intentions, activities are intensified as well as provocations so that the enemy forces would be tied there, and therefore they are rendered unable to send more forces to an area where one does have the intention of accomplishing an objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you returned to the Main Staff, did you see for yourself that from mid-June until the beginning of July the 28th Division was involved in this kind of manoeuvre and operation of tying up our forces?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I arrived, throughout the front line there were a few neuralgic points. On the western side, in the 1st Corps, in the first one in Vlasic, in the East Bosnian Corps around Lisica and -- actually for a long period of time they had one of their companies encircled there. Then the Hercegovina Corps had active operations from the plateau Treskavica and so on. And in June from the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica, nine sabotage groups were sent to an area that was in the immediate vicinity of the Main Staff, and they endangered the Main Staff. And the Communications Regiment and the 65th Regiment sustained heavy losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just be specific. Was my understanding correct that at Lisica our company was encircled for a long time? And in line 5, it seems as if it is their company.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is the -- it is a company of the Eastern Bosnian Corps that was encircled. It is one of our companies.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that -- 4113, 65 ter, and there is a translation as well. Do we agree that this is also a regular report for the 7th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we ask for paragraph 6 again. Could you please focus on the last sentence -- well, actually focus on all of them, but the last one, situation in the Srebrenica enclave, the enemy was involved in regrouping and in Srebrenica, Zeleni Jadar they put up strong defence using all available weapons. And then the situation in the corps, subparagraph (b). There was a selective response by hitting visible targets. The forces intended for active combat operations in the front around Srebrenica have been unable to carry out actions to date due to extremely stormy weather, and so on and so forth. Do you agree that the president has information stating that our forces around Srebrenica are behaving in a regular fashion, that they are opening selective fire at targets that have been observed, and that there is nothing contained in this information that the president should find alarming?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is derived from the content of this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, is this a regular report or an interim report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the beginning it does say "regular report." It's the heading there. Actually, you can display the front page again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this bears the number 03/3-188, and the document we saw earlier on before this document was -- did bear the number 187. So we -- can we take it that this is the very next report that Main Staff sent after the previous one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You can see from the contents that it is a regular combat report and the numbers are sequential, of course. With interim reports, it should be specified in the title that it is interim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I was wondering whether there was a -- there was an interim report between these two regular reports.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interim report does not bear the sequential number. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it was logged in the same book, but the title would be "Interim Report," since there was a ledger for all reports, a book for all reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, if this were indeed an interim report, would it contain information about all the corps or would it only address certain extraordinary events?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it were an interim combat report, it would refer to a specific area and event. It wouldn't refer to general information. It would, rather, focus on an area and a unit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted just before the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be admitted as the next exhibit, Exhibit D2098. My confusion arose from the passage in the previous document which said: "Upon receiving an interim report we will inform you on the combat result achieved so far." It did not say that it will send an interim report to the Presidency. That's how I understood it. And before we break, Ms. Edgerton, when I told you that we'll mark it for identification one intercept among the associated exhibits, I meant 31237A, not 32498, which is to be admitted in full, because Mr. Obradovic himself testified to the content of the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take a break for half an hour and resume at half past -- five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, if we go back to what Judge Kwon said, perhaps we can clarify. Is it possible that the Main Staff receive interim combat reports as well, but even in such cases that information was included into the regular combat reports that were sent to me?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. It depended also on the time that elapsed between the interim report and the last regular report. Perhaps if there is a possibility, that interim report and its information would be incorporated into the next regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have 65 ter 4114 of the 8th of July. Do we agree, General Obradovic, that this seems to be a regular report of the 8th of July? Its number is 189, the next number in line, that is; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go to item 6, please, referring to the Drina Corps. Please look at subparagraph (a), "The Enemy." There seems to be some activity in the area towards Gorazde and Vranovina. The last sentence says the following: "On the part of the front towards Srebrenica, the Tri Sise feature was seized by us." Are these three hills?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are features.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Topographic features.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, elevations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In subparagraph (b) we see "Situation in the corps." The last sentence: "The units who are active around the front on the Srebrenica enclave seized the Tri Sise feature on the axis Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica." So we have the feature again. Is Zeleni Jadar to the south of Srebrenica, between Srebrenica and Zepa which was supposed to have been in our territory? It was not a protected area.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In physical terms it is located between the two enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit D2099.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 4115.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, General Obradovic, that this is the same kind of report but for the 9th of July, 1995? We have the same protocol sequence with the following number in line, which is 109.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One hundred and ninety.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 6 again, please. The Drina Corps. Please look at subparagraph (a), "The Enemy." The last sentence has to do with Srebrenica. "At the front towards Srebrenica, the enemy fired from all types of weapons and heavy weapons." Then "Situation in the corps," subparagraph (b): "The corps units are in full combat readiness." Further below, it says: "The forces conducting active combat operations on the front around the Srebrenica enclave are advancing according to plan." II. "Situation in the territory:" "From the Srebrenica enclave, from the observation post, 15 members of UNPROFOR fled in two vehicles to our territory (Dutch), accommodated at the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac." Is this what the document states and was the president to be supposed to take any note of this or action, either myself or my advisors?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have P4449.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just can we stay on this document. No. Let us proceed. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was admitted as a Prosecution exhibit. Is this also the next report in line of the 10th of July, 1995, with the number 191?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 6 again, please. Please look at sub-item (b), "Our units." It reads: "The corps units are in full combat readiness. The main body of the force is engaged in persistent defence while a part of the forces is engaged in active combat operations, especially around the Srebrenica enclave where they are carrying out combat tasks as planned. Upon receipt of the report from that sector of the front, we will send an interim report."

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that the text on the screen reflects what I have. We received it on the 11th. It should be P4449, which is 65 ter 4116. Yes, this is the right one. Item 6, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is for the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Item 6, please. So it says that the corps units are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not -- yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 6, please. Is this the right one? Yes. So look at sub-item (b). Please zoom in for the General, the Serbian version, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In sub-item (b), we find the following: "The corps units are in full combat readiness. The main body of the force is engaged in persistent defence while a part of the force is engaged in active combat operations, especially around the Srebrenica enclave where they are carrying out combat tasks as planned." The last sentence: "A part of the forces is engaged in the depth of the territory in order to control it." Does that mean that our rear may have been in danger and that there was a possibility of enemy groups being present?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that there is nothing in this report that would make my advisors inform me of any extraordinary or important events?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing. It's just that it says "upon receipt of the report." It seems that from certain units the Drina Corps did not receive their respective reports and they promised to report once they have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has been admitted. Could we have P4450 for the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that, General, do you agree that it where says that they were active according to plan, the plan was to separate the two enclaves and to regain control of the road between Podravanje and Skelani, which was not supposed to be under their control in the first place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The task was to have the enclaves within the arranged borders and to make any communication between the two enclaves impossible, because by that time their communication was quite extensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they used that route to supply weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they were free to make incursions into Serbian villages and carry out actions against Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the 11th of July, item 6, please, the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, what is your basis of knowledge as to the content of the plan? Was it based upon having read documents afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read a directive as well as directive 7.1 later on. I was also shown a number of documents by the Prosecutor, Mr. McCloskey. In any case, the Drina Corps had this constant problem with the forces of the 28th Division which were in immediate tactical vicinity, and there was always this danger that they would join their forces with the 2nd Tuzla Corps of the Army of BiH. It was a standing problem and it figures frequently in the Drina Corps reports and their analysis of combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the last sentence of item 6. The rest of the paragraph refers to other areas of responsibility, whereas this one refers to Srebrenica. It says: "In the area of Srebrenica, there is strong opposition to VRS forces."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could we have the exact reference in the English translation, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Just wait for the interpreters, until they see the reference. You are reading out subparagraph (b).

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. I am now at sub-item (b), and sub-item (a) discussed the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In subparagraph (b), we have a reference to combat readiness. It says that some forces are engaged in offensive operations around the Srebrenica enclave. The last sentence says: "Corps units responded to provocations by firing on observed targets ..." Does this entail military targets that were observed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In military parlance, observed targets are either units or combat groups, as well as positions of military assets. Those are the targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this report of the 11th, was there anything that was supposed to alarm my advisors and that they would request my attention?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. It seems that some of this report is illegible, but it would be convenient if we could see the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to intervene so much. You said, "In this report of the 11th, was there anything that was supposed to alarm my advisors and that they would request my attention?" You said, "No." But in the report it says: "Our forces entered the town of Srebrenica, which was a UN-protected safe haven." Is it not something that warrants alarming the president? Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] President Karadzic did not read out this particular sentence, but I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, General, that the office in Pale received it at 2.20 in the morning on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that reports arrived late. It says that it was received on the 12th of July, 1995, at 2.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the morning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You weren't there, but did they show you a document in which on the 9th in the evening, Krstic informed Tolimir that the conditions had suddenly been created for entry into Srebrenica, and I authorised this with certain restrictions? So this sentence couldn't have surprised me because I had already been informed about the fact that the conditions had been created for entering Srebrenica. Did you see those documents in the course of the preparations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Since I have already -- since I was already informed about that possibility, was it unlawful to enter Srebrenica, which had not been demilitarised? I apologise if this is legally complicated, but you certainly studied international law. If one side violates the agreement on demilitarisation, the other side no longer has to respect that agreement. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The idea of a protected zone entails the idea of demilitarisation. Here it is quite obvious that within the Srebrenica enclave there was the presence of a division, and combat activity was continually carried out from that enclave. We sustained losses. Our troops sustained losses. Inhabitants were killed, cattle was taken away, and houses were set on fire. Given such occurrences, it was our right to prevent such things from happening in the sense that we had to destroy and neutralise the combat formations that were present in the demilitarised -- or, rather, protected zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Does the information according to which we entered Srebrenica mean that we committed any crimes? Was the president informed about the perpetration of crimes of any kind?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the fact that it says that Srebrenica had been entered, there is no other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now see P3054, dated the 12th of July. General, would you agree that here, too, we can see the number 03/3-193, and it's dated the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at item 6 again. Could we see item 6 in the English version, too, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the last sentence under (a): "From the Srebrenica enclave, the enemy tried to pull out together with women and children towards Ravni Buljin and Konjevic Polje, but they ran into a minefield." And (b), a reference is made to the situation in the corps, and the second sentence says: "Engagement of units to carry out the Krivaja 95 operation: All the combat tasks are going ahead as planned. During the day they liberated Potocari and they continue advancing in order to liberate all of the settlements in the Srebrenica enclave. On the axes, part of our units and MUP units have organised ambushes in order to destroy Muslim extremists who have not surrendered and who are trying to break out from the enclave towards Tuzla." Do we agree that in these two sub-items, it's clear that the objective of our army didn't relate to civilians but to Muslim extremists who hadn't surrendered and who were attempting a breakthrough?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says under (b).

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please have a look at III. The situation in the territory. It says: "In the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, the population is being taken by organised transport from Srebrenica towards Kladanj. During the day, about 10.000 Muslims estimated for transport." Does it say driving out, deportation, or evacuation, or does it just say that the population is being transported?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the population is being transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Five days after this event, you went to the Main Staff. In the Main Staff were there any discussions about the forcible deportation of this population or was it quite clear that this was done in agreement with the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no indication that force had been used. I know that there were negotiations with certain representatives of the Muslim people from Srebrenica with regard to that transport. I know this from having watched television. And I think this took place in a hotel in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And given what you heard at the time and subsequently found out in the Main Staff, your understanding was that those who left were people who wanted to leave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just ask you something else very briefly. You're certainly aware of our Law on All People's Defence. General, with regard to combat activities, do you agree that the army has to evacuate the civilian population whether it wants to be evacuated or not? This doesn't mean, however, that they cannot return.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This concerned the area of combat operations. These provisions applied to those areas, but given the way events unfolded, in our situation this was often not possible to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's now have a look at 65 ter document 1917. I think it's been admitted as P4464. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell us whether the date is the 13th of July, and does this number 194 follow this series of numbers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at item 6 once again. In the English version too. Here it mentions Gorazde. And then the next sentence is: "The enemy from the former enclave of Srebrenica is in a state of total disarray, and the troops are surrendering in large numbers to the VRS. A 200- to 300-strong group of soldiers managed to break through to the general sector of Mount Udrc, from where they are trying to break through to the territory under Muslim control." And it mentions our situation, and it says that it concerns combing through the terrain of Srebrenica municipality. Have a look at number 2, situation on the territory. "There is an organised and planned transfer of the population from Srebrenica to the territory under Muslim control." So on the 13th, was it more certain that this was being done in accordance with plans and in a controlled manner?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that at some earlier time there had been plans for Muslims to be transferred from Srebrenica forcibly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
