utterances.text: There was no forcible transfer, but when the protected zone was created and when General Morillon entered the area, well, I think that at the time one UNPROFOR contingent transferred some of the population in accordance with their wishes, but the Sarajevo leadership, in fact, prevented this from being done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that this action taken by the Muslim leadership in Sarajevo, this action taken to prevent civilians from leaving the combat zone, do you agree that this action was a violation of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the right of the inhabitants deciding where they want to be, yes, but as to what their interests were, I don't want to speculate about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that victimising one's own population was an integral part of the military and political leadership of the Muslims? They wanted to victimise their population, portray them as victims in order to gain the sympathy of the international community. Was that the case according to what you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank yo. If we take into consideration the fact that two-thirds of the population in the protected zone at the time did not come from Srebrenica but from other places, does this show that the violation of their rights was even more serious? They were prevented from going somewhere where they wanted to live.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that the local inhabitants of Srebrenica had the right decide to leave that place and not only those who were not originally from the Srebrenica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Could we now see P4457. Could you please have a look at the document. Is it the 14th of July? Is that the date? The same administration. The number is 195. It's the next number in the series in comparison to the previous day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's have a look at item 6 again. Please have a look under item (a), 6(a), "The Enemy." It says: "A major concentration of the enemy forces was noticed. Most probably their objective is to carry out an attack and join up with the groups which are currently pulling out of Srebrenica." So there were a number of groups, and they were massing in order to link up with each other; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now have a look at (b), where it says: "Corps units are maintaining the ordered level of combat readiness. The main body of the corps is engaged in defence, whereas the Milici and Bratunac Brigades as well as the Skelani Independent Infantry Battalion are scouring the terrain and receiving a large number of Muslim fugitives who are surrendering to them." So do these Muslims have to do with the concentration of enemy forces or are they civilians? So does this term, does this expression concern soldiers, the term "Muslim fugitives." The expression "Muslim fugitives," how do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, given the inconsistency in the vocabulary, in the vocabulary used, I can't really say. If I had written this, I would have either stated that soldiers were concerned or civilians, but Muslim fugitives is often used as a general expression for a member of enemy forces. No distinction is made between civilians and troops, so I really can't speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. But under item (a) enemy forces are mentioned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this means soldiers, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could we see P4460. Have a look at the number 03/3-9196, and date is the 15th of July -- or, rather, the number is 196 and the date is the 15th of July; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we have a look at item 6 again. The first part is about the other Caparde sector, the Caparde sector. Do you agree that in the first sentence it says that the enemy opened fire from the direction of the 2nd -- from the area of the 2nd Corps from Kalesija on the units in the Gornja Caparde sector? Do you agree that this is co-operation with forces that are breaking through from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That part of the front faced Tuzla, Kalesija, Zivinice, so from Karakaj, Zvornik over Caparde and further on in the direction of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But that was also legitimate action. It wasn't expected that the president should do something, because it is the enemy's legitimate right to launch an attack. Isn't that correct? Although it could be reason for concern.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Joint action can also take place when there isn't physical contact between units. These units leaving from Srebrenica, they were in our rear, whereas these others are units at the front facing Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it says: "The remains of the broken up Muslim formations from the former Srebrenica enclave moving towards Kravica and Konjevic Polje in order to move on to the Udrc mount area and from there to Tuzla and Zivinice. During the course of today's day, several enemy groups have surrendered to VRS members in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. Around 0440 hours, the enemy launched a strong artillery attack on the defence lines. The attack ended 05 -- 530 hours, but the enemy continued opening artillery and small arms fire at short intervals. During transport towards Zvornik, the Turkish troops pulling out from Srebrenica towards Tuzla opened fire on an ambulance in -- and killed the driver of the vehicle and a paramedic." General, does this relate to our rear and about significant clashes that occurred on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These forces that were crushed means that there were several smaller combat units involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, do we agree that nothing unusual is being stated here? There is no reference to crimes, nothing that would require efforts to be made by the president?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part there is no such reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have II. I think that in Serbian it's on the next page. And in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, General, that it says: "Situation in the territory, the Vlasenica-Zvornik road is unsafe due to enemy groups from Srebrenica which are trying to break through to Tuzla." So the main road through that area is unsafe because there are combat groups there; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You hadn't arrived yet, but you have information concerning the following: The local leadership was afraid, and on the 14th of July, I declared a state of war there in Podrinje because -- because there was a lack of seriousness on the part of Serbs, and these groups could have taken Milici, Zvornik, whatever. Did you hear that there was a partial declaration of state of war only on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was carried by the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have a look at 65 ter 1920. Again, briefly for identification purposes. It's the same administration. The date is the 16th, and the number is one up, 197; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move on to paragraph 6 again. And this is the 16th of July. Could we have paragraph 6. And now let us please focus on what it says about the Drina Corps, subparagraph (a). [As read] "On the Tuzla-Zvornik axis, the enemy in front of the PK" --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Front end."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- "grouped major forces and used them early in the morning in a stronger artillery and infantry attack on our unit's sector along the Baljkovicka-Rijeka-Pandurica axis. They were coordinating" --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Coordinating."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see, "coordinating with the forces pulling out from the former Srebrenica enclave. They were able to break through the defence and capture three trenches in the Baljkovici village sector, create a corridor for the pull-out of the civilian population which was used by about 7.000 mainly unarmed civilians, men, women, children. During this attack the enemy attacked our units from behind the lines irrespective of own losses. Thus they captured three self-propelled guns by bodies, losing hundreds of soldiers. We are currently negotiating with the Muslims with regard to freeing the captured policemen and members of the Zvornik Brigade and the duration of the corridor in the Kalesija-Kladanj part of the front, the enemy carried out provocations," and so on and so forth. Do we agree, General, that this is the first report dated the 16th of July informing me that in that column that was breaking through there were civilians as well, that these civilians, except perhaps in the first report, were not mentioned as part of the column?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So could this also pacify my advisors that they had gotten through, so that they could not alarm me? They had gotten through?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since they had gotten through, there was nothing special, nothing specially dramatic, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move on to the next page in Serbian. Subparagraph (b). Did you find out -- this was the day before you arrived. Did you find out that they used bodies to take our weapons and equipment and that we had both sustained major losses?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about the dramatic situation in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. I was not aware of any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please focus on subparagraph (b). The corps units are in full combat readiness. The 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade and attached units are fighting the Muslims who pulled out of Srebrenica. They are trying to deblock the -- they are actually trying to block the Muslim units in order proceed and destroy these groups. The 1st Milici Brigade and the 1st Bratunac Brigade and the Skelani Infantry Battalion forces are searching the terrain with the objective of neutralising remaining enemy groups. General, on the basis of your own military training, is all of this legitimate military activity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, you said -- can my voice be heard?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I don't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Turn off your microphone. Could you hear me now? I will use my colleague's. General Obradovic, you said you heard about the dramatic situation in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. What did you mean by "dramatic situation in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is dramatic is that in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade, that is to say, in the area of Zvornik, there were quite a few armed groups of Muslims in a large area, and they did not have enough forces to control the area. So that was dangerous for the civilian population in that area, in that area of responsibility, because they did not know when they went to work or when they took a car, whatever, whether they would come across them, especially because there were cases of these attacks that took place on roads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, when you say "they did not have enough forces to control the territory," you mean the Zvornik Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is its area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2101, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I was informed that your microphone, Excellency, is not in function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. My doesn't work, but we can proceed. I will use my colleague's.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 4005.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Again, 03/3-198. The same report; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6, please. Please take a look at this. This is the usual reference to Kalesija, all over that part of the front line, that the enemy is active intermittently, but under II, could you please take a look at the Drina Corps. In the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, the territory is being searched and they are capturing and destroying groups that pulled out of the former Srebrenica enclave. Are you aware of the fact that these are their armed groups or, rather, combatants?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2102, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly cast a glance at P4459.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, General, that everything is as usual except the number is 199 and the date is --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Subparagraph (a), could we have a look at that now. Gorazde, Sopotnica, and the rest. We don't have to deal with that. Srebrenica, rather. "Crushed enemy forces from the former Srebrenica enclave have been trying to break towards Tuzla in smaller groups. They have been using the following axes: Pobrdje-Kaldrmica-Udrc and Udrc-Brezik-Caparde. In the general sector of Kamenica, the presence of new enemy groups and civilians has been discovered. Allegedly one of their brigades has still not managed to pull out according to our -- enemy forces have been withdrawing one brigade after the other in a rather organised manner with the support of forces from the front line and stronger artillery support, which has inflicted major losses on our units." Do we agree, first of all, that this report makes a distinction between enemy groups and civilians, whereby enemy groups are soldiers and civilians does not mean anything -- or, rather, does not mean the enemy?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. So this is the 18th of July. There is at least one brigade in our rear, and there is also fighting on the front line facing Tuzla; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems here that this is new information, that they were withdrawing one brigade after the other, and according to estimates made here, one brigade was still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this brigade and enemy groups are the target of our army, not civilians. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at subparagraph (c) now. "During combat operations with Muslim formations which have been pulling out of Srebrenica, in the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade we've had the following losses: 27 dead, 24 seriously wounded, 72 lightly wounded, 13 wounded, and a captured officer." In a single day, in a single brigade, are these not immense losses, General, in a brigade that is defending itself, that is part of a defence formation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are great losses. Over a short span of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does -- is this part of these dramatic developments in the area of responsibility of that brigade that you heard of?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is included but also the situation in the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You did hear, right, that our civilians fell victim to these groups that had not been noticed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that one vehicle was affected, a few policemen, and then this ambulance. I cannot remember many details now, but that's what made it so dramatic and so uncertain for the population in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General Obradovic. P4416, can we now have that document, please. Please, can you confirm that yet again this is 03/3-200, on the 19th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I please have paragraph 6 again. 6, subparagraph (a), it says: "Enemy. In the zone of responsibility of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, formations from the Srebrenica enclave were smashed and surrounded in Planinci and Baljkovici villages. In the sectors of Bijela Zemlja and Gornja Kamenica, enemy groups are attempting to break through Muslim-controlled territory." So do you agree on the 19th of July there is still intensive fighting going on there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this report included, there is nothing that was supposed to alarm the president or his advisors; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about you, but to us this situation and the losses were alarming. It was our military task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree, General, but I wanted to ask you this: Is there any information here about any illegal or criminal activities that the president should be aware of?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we next have 65 ter 4017. Three days later, the 22nd of July, and three numbers later, 203.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 22nd of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There were reports in between, but nothing of relevance happened in the past three days. Can we go again to item 6? If there was anything of relevance, the number would not be 203.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In English it is page 4 and 5. Please look at sub-item (b) where the 1st Zvornik Brigade is mentioned. "The 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade organised a search of the terrain, destruction and capture of the remaining enemy groups and individuals." Further down below it says: "In Gavrici village, an enemy group which tried to pass through the defence line was smashed. Two enemy soldiers were liquidated and the rest were dispersed by fire by the Zvornik MUP units. On Nedzuk, Boskovici, and Medjedja, enemy artillery fire was prevented. In the Rudnik sector, 17 enemy soldiers were captured, and in the Spreca sector, two enemy soldiers were captured." The first question, General. It says "the rest were dispersed." Does it mean that they fled, they were not captured or killed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It means they dispersed, broke away from this compact unit or group. They were neither killed nor captured or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree, General, that on the 22nd of July, the situation was still quite dangerous with a lot of combat going on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was it not already admitted? Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2103, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have 65 ter 4020?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us identify the report briefly. The number is 204. The date the 23rd of July, a day later than the previous report.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 6 again, please. Sub-item (a), enemy information. There's a reference to the Milici and Bratunac Brigade. It says: "Part of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, 1st ZP, and 1st Birac Infantry Brigade are still searching and mopping up the terrain of the remaining enemy groups and individuals. In the Baljkovici-Mihajlovic sector, the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade zone of responsibility, about 20 enemy soldiers were captured. The soldiers of the 1st Bratunac Brigade captured two enemy soldiers. We have been carrying out active combat operations with part of our forces around the Zepa enclave." This term "mopping up," does it mean mopping up the remaining or straggling enemy groups and even without that further explanation, it entailed the mopping up of a certain area to remove any enemy soldiers, not civilians.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In military parlance, the term of "search and mopping up" of the terrain is used. "Mopping up" refers to armed soldiers of the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it is indicated that activities are carried out only against enemy soldiers and military targets. So it's all legitimate; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2104, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 65 ter 3972.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us identify it. The number is 207, the 26th of July. So there must have been reports 204, 205, and 206, but we found nothing of interest there. Is this the 26th of July, number 207?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 6, please. In English it is page 4. Look at sub-item (b): "Situation in the corps. Units have continued carrying out defensive operations" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "The corps units."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- "are holding the current positions tightly. They are taking measures against surprise actions especially against enemy groups from Srebrenica. Units engaged in Zepa are securing the evacuation of the Muslim population." In other words, they are not the ones carrying out the evacuation but securing it; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It also specifies that all Drina Corps unit's activities are legitimate and of military nature. Can we conclude anything to the contrary from what we see in the document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So securing the evacuation is a duty on our part and it was a part of regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2105, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps instead of "security" we can have it interpreted as "safety." If the interpreters could confirm. "Securing" is used as a verb, whereas in the original we have a noun, "safety."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That may be looked into later on, but, Mr. Karadzic, given that my microphone is not working, how about taking a break now for an hour during which I would like the technicians to take a look into it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I have three remaining documents on this topic and then we could break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have 65 ter 4027, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, the 27th, the number 209.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the 28th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise. So the 28th of July. The number is 209; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 6, please. Sub-item (a). It mentions certain positions at Boskovici, et cetera, which was in the direction of Tuzla, between Tuzla and Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says in the area of other brigades there was no combat, although routed groups that came out of Srebrenica were sighted. Sub-item B, situation in the corps: "Our units are in full combat readiness. They are engaged in intensive reconnaissance and monitoring in order to uncover and destroy routed enemy groups. They are erecting barricades and laying ambushes." Is this legitimate military activity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are no indications that actions were aimed at the population or illegitimate targets.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2106, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next, could we have 1 -- 65 ter 13694.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, is this the 6th of August, the number of the report is 218; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 6 again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: If there is a translation in English, we would like to have it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have the English translation, do we?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Then could we kindly ask the accused to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there is translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it, General, sub-item (a), let's not dwell on that. Sub-item (b), I will read it out loud. "In the area of the village of Kamenica, the forces of the 5th Light Infantry Brigade came across an enemy group moving from the direction of Zepa during which occasion they killed three enemy soldiers. The laying of ambushes and search of terrain continues as well as pursuit of the broken-up enemy groups." This is the 6th of August. Do you agree, General that this, too, was legitimate military activity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted -- MFI'd. There is no translation. There was not enough time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D2107, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last document is 65 ter 16565, also no translation. It is still pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Again let us identify it. The 11th of July, and the number is 223.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sorry. The 11th of August. Item 6, please. Sub-item (a), "The Enemy:" "Straggling enemy groups from the former enclave of Srebrenica tried to pull out through the area of the 1st Bratunac Infantry Brigade and were discovered in a timely manner." In sub-item (b), we have the following: "During the day, seven enemy soldiers tried to pull out towards Tuzla. Units continue with the search of terrain." It's not clear what happened with the seven enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since they were trying to go to Tuzla, they were probably trying to move in that direction, to break through to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. And it seems that on our side there was one killed. The II: "In the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, late in the evening on the 10th of August, 1995, in the area of Ruzina Voda, along the road to Vlasenica, a policeman was killed and his wife wounded, probably by some enemy soldiers pulling out. On that occasion, an enemy soldier was killed." So there was nothing in the area. There was no one in the area that was safe from these enemy soldiers, and it actually happened a full month after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because they dispersed across a very large area and no one was safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, can this be admitted, and we can then go on our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll mark it for identification as Exhibit D2108.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, can we have a shorter break in order to be able to wrap things up with General Obradovic today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not practicable. Shall we break for 50 minutes? I think that -- if that's agreeable. So we'll resume at 20 past 1.00. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 1.20. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.28 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, let us conclude the following -- the previous topic. Do you agree that in all the reports we presented, the president and his office had not been informed about a single crime?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking about analyses of combat readiness on the basis of which directives are made, on page 13 of yesterday's transcript, you confirmed that an analysis of combat readiness for the previous year is conducted in the following way: The corps present what they did, they envisage what it is that they should do, and they make proposals. Someone from that service collects these proposals from this meeting and includes them in the draft directive; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Some directives are signed by the commander of the Main Staff, and others were signed to the president, for the president to sign?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General Obradovic, now I'd like to ask you something as a matter of principle. If a superior officer makes a mistake, intentionally or unintentionally, does the subordinate officer have the right not to carry out an erroneous decision? Does he have the right to correct it, but before that he has to inform his superior officer about that; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the principles and rules that we took over from the JNA, orders are carried out correctly and in a timely fashion, except if one receives an order whose implementation would constitute a crime. In that case, the person who receives such an order is duty-bound not to carry out the said order and to report to his second reporting officer about the kind of order he had received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this person should report that he had received an erroneous decision that he would not carry out, and he provides information as to why he's not going to carry it out; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A subordinate commander at any level, is he authorised to change a decision without informing anybody about that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He doesn't have the right to change a decision without providing information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You confirmed to us that at the time when directive 7 was created and signed you were not in the Main Staff on the 8th of March, and you said that you did not take part in this. However, in the Tolimir case -- or, rather, Popovic case, you confirmed that the directive for the participants -- this is 22355, that's the 65 ter number, and the page is 28303 to 307. So a draft was made, so the person who was the drafter unified all the elements -- or, rather, made them uniform, and -- actually, those elements that this person had received from all the other organs that took part in drafting that document, and that is how the document is created; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The person whose name is written at the end of the directive where it says "Compiled by," this person basically collects the completed elements of the directive from the organs of the command that are in charge of writing certain elements, and this person then forms a single document out of all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So something that would pertain to the Drina Corps in a particular directive, that would be derived from the presentation of what the Drina Corps had done and the proposals as to what it should do in the forthcoming period; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within this analysis, through the discussion or a summary that is presented by the corps commander. He presents this by way of conclusions and he proposes what the tasks would be in the forthcoming period. The extent to which this will be adopted depends on his superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that a directive is a document of strategy and principle and that, later on, the Main Staff and lower commands turn it into executive orders, but the directive itself is not an executive order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the hearing yesterday, I communicated the definition of a directive, that this is a combat document of high commands and staffs, and in it elements are provided for a longer period of time for the preparation and implementation of combat operations. Tasks are not spelled out in detail in directives. Rather, the objectives of operations are pointed out, the general task of the unit in the spirit of the commander's idea. So a directive provides elements to subordinate commands for them to carry out their planning and execution of combat operations independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you about directive number 7. Do you know that directive number 7 was transformed into an executive order by General Mladic, that is 7-1, and in it he changed certain controversial elements from directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I compared the documents that were given to me in the previous trial by Mr. McCloskey, I compared the tasks from directive 7 and directive 7-1, and the task of the Drina Corps is not identical in these two directives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Mladic changed something in directive 7, and that something is not contained in directive 7-1; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Directive 7-1 that was signed by the commander of the Main Staff -- I mean, the content of the task of the Drina Corps are not identical to those in directive 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In accordance with the principles of command and control, could Mladic change this at his own initiative, or did he have to know that it had come from me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpretation is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is my question: If Mladic were to believe that this had come from me, he would not dare change this until he would inform me about it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. He would have to seek approval for a change of directive 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, if his understanding was that this had come from some services and that it was a mistake, he did not have to inform me. He could have changed it; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how he made his conclusions, but that is probably the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now -- now I would like to ask you to take a look at this, how this directive 7-1, which is executive, affected the area of the Drina Corps, particularly Srebrenica, especially in relation to humanitarian aid. Now I'm going to present to you briefly and quickly what humanitarian aid was like, say, from September 1993 until just before the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could General Obradovic please be shown 1D05365.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you a time sequence. And let us see whether there were any changes in our position regarding humanitarian issues and whether that was a change for the better or for the worse. Please focus on this, where it says "Srebrenica." Do we agree that the command of the 1st Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade on the 25th of September, 1993, received approval from the Main Staff for 80 metric tonnes to enter Srebrenica? 80 metric tonnes of some humanitarian aid from the UNHCR. And then for Srebrenica and Sarajevo, a Russian convoy, 90 and 80 tonnes. So the plans are on a weekly basis. Do we agree with that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we move on to the next page. Do we agree that on the 1st of October it is 80 tonnes, and on the 2nd of October, Sarajevo, 80 metric tonnes of food, and it was signed by the Chief of Staff, General Manojlo Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? For identification. The translation's not there yet, but it's a question of numbers. So it's easy to understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Obradovic, did you say the 1st Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade received the approval? Where do we see Zvornik Brigade? Can we see the first page again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff informed all corps. However, this particular check-point in Zvornik received --

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2109, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D05366. There is a translation. However, it's numbers, so whatever you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, again it's a weekly plan for Srebrenica, the 5th of October, 100 metric tonnes. On the 6th of October, 80 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't think the -- this is a correct translation. I see IBK, HK, SRK, but we see only Drina Corps. Date is different.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a mistake in the translation or it's the wrong document, but since this only concerns numbers, Your Excellency, we'll correct that. I just wanted to introduce the document to the General so that he can confirm a few things. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, do you agree that on the 5th of October, a hundred metric tonnes were approved for Srebrenica and 65 for Zepa?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 6th, 80 metric tonnes for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 8th, 80 tonnes for Sarajevo, and on the 9th for Sarajevo 80 tonnes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next page, please. The 10th, Sarajevo, 90 tonnes; Srebrenica, 100 tonnes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Gorazde 65.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it says the following: "The approval pertains exclusively to the supply of food, medication, medical material, and material for hygiene. Any other material cannot be transported to the Muslim territory without a separate approval of which you will be informed in time."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters did not hear the answer nor the following remark by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters were not able to catch up the last part of the question and answer. First, could you repeat your answer, General Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please -- [Microphone not activated] please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.text: As MFI D2110, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 1D105367. We will have two more documents for 1993 and then we'll move on to 1995, before and after directive 7.9. So 1D105367.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is dated the 8th of October, weekly report to all corps, and this one was received in the Zvornik Brigade as we can see on the stamp; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 11th of October, Srebrenica 80 metric tonnes. The 13th of October, Foca, 83; Srebrenica 65. On the 14th of October, Srebrenica, 65 metric tonnes. In the text following the figures it says: "The approval pertains exclusively to the supply of food, medical supplies and toiletries." Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Signed by Colonel Miletic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2111, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The last document from 1993, which is 1D05 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1D105368.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another weekly plan sent to all corps. This one was received by the Zvornik military post in Cyrillic. Do we agree?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 18th of October, 65 metric tonnes for Srebrenica. The 20th of October, 100 metric tonnes for Srebrenica. The 21st of October, 80 metric tonnes for Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next page, please. The 23rd of October, Sarajevo, 80 metric tonnes. The 24th of October, again Sarajevo, 80 metric tonnes. So two days in a row. The box towards the bottom says: "The approval pertains exclusively to the supply of food, toiletries, and medical supply. Any other material cannot be transferred to the Muslim territory without a separate approval of which you will be notified in time." It seems that this sentence keeps appearing in the same context.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what they repeated in every plan.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a standing clause. I believe that's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Correct, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to January 1995, 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this one be admitted, first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, 2112, Exhibit D2112.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D05373. I'll have to skip many for the lack of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this another weekly plan of the 19th of January, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Gorazde, 5.600 litres of oil. And then we have Karakaj and Srebrenica, for the 21st of January, 5.600 litres of heating oil. Then the 24th, 9 trucks with 72 metric tonnes of food and one truck of 5.600 litres of heating oil. You can see the figures for the 25th, 9 trucks.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 72 tonnes.

utterances.text: Yes. 180 rolls of plastic foil, 4 cans of glue, 15 boxes of men's clothes, and 72 boxes of children's clothes, and we have some other data we can see all that; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next page, please. Here we have Zepa and other locations. Let's look at the bottom. "The convoy leader will be in possession of original approvals under the specific numbers and appropriate documentation about the cargo as well as the vehicles and persons involved. Exercise control and enable them to move freely along the specified travel routes." Signed by Milovanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2113, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D035374, please. We'll skip another few.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is another weekly plan starting with the 16th of February, 1995? The Hercegovina and Drina Corps commands were informed because they had their check-points in the area of the convoy; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at the 18th of February. Gorazde and then Srebrenica, 9 motor vehicles, 15 metric tonnes of flour, 8 metric tonnes of beans, 392 boxes of beef. Well, you can see it for yourself. Then on the same day, one tank truck with 5.600 litres of heating oil; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The upper one was to come from Uzice and Serbia proper, whereas the other one was to go via Karakaj and Srebrenica, the one in the box.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's why they informed the Hercegovina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at the 21st. Karakaj, Srebrenica, 9 motor vehicles, 23 metric tonnes of flour, 5 tonnes of beans. And on the 22nd we have something similar, another tank truck, pillows, et cetera; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2114, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D05391, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that this is a weekly report of the approved convoys between the 18th of March, 1995, onwards, that is to say, ten days following the famous directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at the quantities to see if directive 7 influenced them. On the 18th, for Srebrenica, 9 trucks, 72 metric tonnes of flour, sugar, powder milk, detergent. On the 26th, there is something for Gorazde, and on the 26th for Srebrenica as well, 10 trucks, 80 metric tonnes, again flour, sugar, et cetera, and on the 22nd of March, 9 trucks, 72 metric tonnes flour, and another tank truck with heating oil; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are the quantities the same as before directive 7? Well, maybe they were not identical, but there were no reductions, if you recall the previous figures.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the number trucks and tonnes tally. They're approximately the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there were no reductions; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard General Milovanovic being criticised for failing to reduce the number -- the quantities of aid for Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have 1D05397, the following weekly plan of the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that it was foreseen and approved that on the 15th of April there are 9 trucks for Srebrenica, 72 metric tonnes of flour, sugar, oil, soap. Then on the 16th, Gorazde and then Srebrenica, seven trucks, 20 metric tonnes. On the 18th, again 9 trucks, 72 metric tonnes of flour, fish, et cetera, and one tank truck of 5.600 litres of heating oil, and two trucks, in brackets (the Swedish construction project). The 19th, 9 trucks, 72 metric tonnes of flour, oil, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, if I told you that there were witnesses here who testified that for months on end convoys did not arrive, would you tell them that they did not state the truth, to say the least?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't need to say anything. It's all here.
