utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that the previous one, the previous document of 7 of April is a duplicate of document that has been already admitted. If the Registrar, for the record, could pronounce the name, the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's Exhibit P839.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll admit this, 1D5397.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll deal with the rest on another occasion since we had to skip them now. Could we have 1D5380 next. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this another weekly plan of the 30th of April, 1994 -- 1995? On the 2nd of May for Srebrenica, nine trucks, then another two trucks. Then on the 3rd of May, nine trucks, and finally, the 4th of May, 18 trucks -- no, 2 trucks and 18 metric tonnes for the Swedish construction project, but the rest is food; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's another duplicate, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Of what exhibit, Ms. Edgerton?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 02068.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we see 1D05400. We have skipped quite a few.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Which is a duplicate of P04452.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I agree. But what -- the Serbian version that was admitted was underlined, and you can't see it very clearly. That is why I wanted this more legible document for the General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the 2nd of June, General. Do we agree that nine lorries entered Srebrenica, and then on 6th of June, nine lorries, on the 7th of June, ten lorries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has been admitted, yes. Just a minute. Could we have a look at P4452. 03702. We'll call that one up. This hasn't been admitted. 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Have a look at this, General. On the 12th of June, do we agree that at the time the offensive around Sarajevo had already started as well as the action around Srebrenica? So this was the second part of June, and it was a very intense period. There's a mistake here. Can you see that it says the 13th of June and then the 14th of June and then the 15th of June. On those three days, eight lorries entered, ten lorries and then two lorries, 72 metric tonnes of goods, 80 metric tonnes, and 30 metric tonnes over this three-day period. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2117, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see 1D05403.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this is a weekly UNHCR plan? It was approved. It's for Srebrenica. The date is the 19th of June. It's for Srebrenica, 72 metric tonnes, 9 lorries, and you can see the goods concerned, soap and so on and so forth. On the 21st of June, another nine lorries were supposed to deliver goods to Srebrenica and the other zones, Gorazde, and so on and so forth. Is that quite clearly stated here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are the same quantities concerned? Were there any changes as a result of directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nine lorries of food and 72 metric tonnes being delivered. Usually the goods concerned flour and beans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2118, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 1D05405.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While waiting for that, General, do you remember that on the 26th of June, Naser Oric's forces went on one of their excursions to the Visnjica village. They torched it, they killed the civilians, and they themselves reported that the Chetniks had sustained civilian losses.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date but I am aware of that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, regardless of the fact, the Main Staff provided authorisation, and on the 4th of July, nine lorries were allowed to go to Gorazde, and for Srebrenica, eight lorries containing the same goods. So the crime they committed didn't have any particular result. You can see that something was delivered to Zepa as well. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't risen yet, but I actually think the questions asked of the witness and answers given for a while now don't even meet the most basic -- come up to the most basic threshold for the -- threshold test for admissibility of these documents. The question asked in this case was with regard to some activities of Naser Oric and so the crime they committed didn't have any particular result. You can see that asking was delivered to Zepa as well. Do you agree with that? And I actually don't think that's sufficient, and it hasn't been sufficient for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Absolutely agree. That's an unnecessary statement on the part of the accused, which has become his habit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise, Your Excellency, but I wanted to refresh everyone's memory in these proceedings. On the 26th -- on the 20th of June, there was a massacre in the village of Visnjica. The Chamber and the Prosecution is aware of the fact as well as the General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're just simply ruining the probative value, if any, of the witness's evidence. Just concentrate on questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I won't ask you about Visnjica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, on the 30th of June, was it planned that on the 4th of July these eight lorries with 65 metric tonnes of goods should enter Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And 9 lorries for Gorazde with 72 tonnes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2119.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D05382.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, General, that this is a weekly plan for delivering -- for delivery? It was drawn up on the 7th of July, 1991, and according to the plan, on the 11th of July, 9 -- 8 lorries with 64 tonnes of flour to enter Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I can leave this for the closing argument, but, General, if you are in the Main Staff and you were planning to enter Srebrenica, would you have issued this sort of authorisation for a convoy that is supposed to provide flour on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, this is intended for the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So was the civilian population then to be evacuated or were they to be provided with food in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing of the sort had been planned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2120, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we see 1D5378 now. Unfortunately, the translation service didn't agree to translate it because they didn't think it was legible enough, but I hope that you will be able to read through it. It's an important document, because it's one week after the directive.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, if the translation service didn't agree to translate it, that means that we're not going to get a translation, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll try whether the witness would be able to read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- please read through it. Do you agree that this was written to me from the Main Staff on the 15th of March, 1995? It was one week after the directive.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Republika Srpska." That's the heading. 06/19-29, dated the 15th of March, 1995, to the President of Republika Srpska. Then the letter starts with the words "Mr. President."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What you can see encircled under number 1 -- or, rather, in the box under number 1 is that legible?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1. "The Doctors Without Borders have organised Western intelligence services in which they have integrated intelligence officers, 'working visits.' In the enclaves" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In function?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the enclaves reports are being received by -- or from operations officers in the field."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Operations officers in the field?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Giving instructions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Giving instructions for intelligence work and to," something, "enclaves," but I don't know what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you have a look at item 2. Is it true that here General Milovanovic, and we'll see that he signed it, General Milovanovic says that lately -- can you read this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the same time we are informing you that with regard to the delivery of humanitarian aid to the enclaves, lately the number of lorries in the convoys has increased, and they are making these deliveries on the basis of weekly plans of the UNHCR" -- I can't read the last part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the UNHCR Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Would General Milovanovic inform me of the fact that the number of convoys was being increased if the week prior to that, I issued an order to reduce the number of convoys? Is this inconsistent? Is this illogical? If it is taken we wanted to reduce the number of convoys, would the General have then informed one of the fact that the number of convoys was being increased?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is illogical.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In fact, I apologise. There is another paragraph. Can you see this part?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Given the number of inhabitants in the enclaves at this time, at this point in time, the enclaves are being provided with supplies, various kinds of supplies and sufficient quantities of the" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Food?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Of food. "In our assessment, amassing more food would be for the intensive preparations of the Muslims to," something -- well, it has to do with their preparations, with their further plans. Thank you. Perhaps General Milovanovic would be able to read this document more easily.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, do you have an objection to marking it for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I take it you mean marked for identification subject to a full and complete translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Otherwise, it will not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All we've been trying to do is have a read of the document, and I actually take issue with the accuracy of the rendering that we've been given in court. Unless there's some threshold question, Your Honour, again I don't think we're there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you started by asking questions about convoy to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour, but for -- in each case with respect to each document, there was some threshold foundational questions with respect to the document itself. We haven't had that. We've only had the witness trying to read illegible portions of the document in this case. That's why I suggest it's different in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2121, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To help Ms. Edgerton, General, in the Main Staff, was the will of the political leadership to reduce humanitarian aid ever thought about, was it ever discussed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at 65 ter 15712. A 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for planning purpose, Ms. Edgerton, I take it you need some time for your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Right now minimum half an hour, I figure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then I shouldn't be rushing through all of this. Then we'd have to ask the General to stay until Monday. It would really be a pity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a separate matter, Mr. Karadzic. I don't think you have spent your time very efficiently so far. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, General, do you remember that I was informed in the previous document that Doctors Without Borders were not clean, as it were, that there were intelligence services involved there? Now, please take a look at this document that is signed by Momir Nikolic, a captain from Bratunac. Do you see that there is a reference here to this abuse, that tools and material appeared, purportedly for the waterworks, and this Captain Nikolic is suggesting that this should be taken away on a permanent basis so that they would no longer be involved in smuggling, because they say that this is taken away when entering the enclaves and then returned when they leave the enclaves? Do you agree that this is yet further proof of abuse in and by the enclaves?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm really wondering why you are putting this document to this witness while you didn't when Mr. Nikolic was here, and this witness knows nothing about this. He knows as much as just we know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Excellency, this was sent to the Main Staff. It arrived in the Main Staff, and the learned Madam Edgerton asked this witness what the army had to do with crisps, potato chips, and we are going to show that potato chips and all sorts of other things were used for smuggling ammunition that was then fired at our people. So the topic was brought up by Ms. Edgerton. I mean, why convoys were being checked. Let us see why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let us proceed. Yes. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2122, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 15706.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, just for planning purposes, we should rise at 3.00 sharp because of another hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, please take a look at this. I don't know whether the translation has arrived. I think it hasn't. Do you agree that this is information on abuse of the mandate of international organisations, and then the dates are for 1993, and it says what they brought in. And look at this, the 13th of October, Karakaj. It's the area of the Drina Corps. So this is just the area of the Drina Corps at Zvornik and Bratunac. Do you agree that the quantities involved in this report are very large, satellite antennas as well, and various material? Look at this, the 13th of October, communications equipment and so on and so forth. On the first page we see that there are about 10 or 15 cases of abuse. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written on this page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that nitrate fertilizer can be used to make explosives, and indeed, explosives were made that way?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, although I'm no expert for explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 11th of December, in the middle of December, 56 tonnes of fertilizer. It is not exactly the farming season, is it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in our part of the world, that climate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read this out. Look at this: Oxygen bottles up here. And then 112 furnaces, a truck of footwear, and then "secera" for Srebrenica. And then further down, it says there were cases when entire UNPROFOR or UNHCR convoys were returned because they refused to be submitted to checks. Probably they had goods that had not been approved. These attempts lead to the conclusion that they were trying to transfer goods to the Muslim side and that this was done by individuals from convoys or entire teams for the purpose of smuggling and so on and so forth. And then there are also cases when they sympathise the Muslim side and therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we are not able to read this, and you are not giving evidence. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Exactly on that point, Your Honour. If Dr. Karadzic is going to read that out, perhaps then he could tell us what parts he's reading and actually read it out instead of paraphrasing as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was in a hurry. I was rushing through it. I wanted to read it, but the essence is faithfully represented. I read it faithfully and then that was the first part. And the second part, the second part of goods that they tried to transport in UNPROFOR convoys or convoys of humanitarian organisations, it can be stated that this was a preconceived operation on the part of members of these organisations who are inclined toward the Muslim side or they wanted to help them with goods that were deficient and that should be used for the needs of the armed forces of the Muslims first and foremost. And then further on it says when the representatives of these organisations complain about the action of organs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not really conducive to an efficient hearing. I don't see the point of time being used in this way. We can't follow at all. Could you not put it in a simpler form to the witness and just let us mark it for identification if it satisfies us as regards the threshold of admission.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, yesterday you were asked about what guided the Main Staff in restricting goods and checking what was brought in. Is this one of the elements that made our army cautious? I mean, these abuses. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I provided an answer yesterday. There were individual cases of abuse, and that led to suspicion on our part, and here a particular organ is referring to a particular area, and he is referring to all of these cases of abuse in his area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted or marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D2123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D5135, can we have a look at that? I am sorry that all of this is due to that challenge regarding potato chips. So this hasn't been translated either, but the General will be able to identify this, and it's the last bit from this series.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, could you please read this. Is it correct that this is being written to Delic, General Delic, in 1992, and can you introduce this document, just the first paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is this stamp in the upper right-hand corner, Ministry of Defence, Army of BH, strictly confidential, 02152-618. The date is the 12th of December, 1992, Sarajevo. So it was received by this institution and it says to Rasim Delic personally, and then Lemos M -- oh, Lemes. And then it has to do with remarks regarding the delivery of goods and oxygen and guidelines for the next delivery on the basis of this instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you read the first bullet point to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We are very seriously objecting to the way you put ammunition into bottles. It is only by sheer coincidence that this time we have not been discovered, because ammunition was rattling every time we moved the bottles. Please pack this ammunition in appropriate sacks as had been the case with a few of these bottles. So in the future nothing should be heard coming from the bottles when they are being moved."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To save time for the Prosecution, I'm not going to ask the General to read out the rest. When the entire document is translated, then you will see what kind of manipulation were is involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sorry, let me just ask you one more thing. Was this not clear to us that this was the way things were being smuggled, under the guise of medical aid?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Our suspicions were based on this kind of thing and knowledge thereof, also, our reservations regarding these convoys.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification as D2124.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D05390, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, now you're going to see the document. It says on the 12th of March, 1995, that is to say, four days after the well-known directive 7.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please enlarge this a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It seems that only the accompanying text has been translated, what the General wrote. The rest is all in Latin, and it's medication. So look at this. Ampicillin, 1.000 boxes. Yes, yes, please just take a look at this. It's thousands and thousands of tablets or injections that were approved. This is a list of medication for Srebrenica that is being transported on the 14th of March, 1993 -- or, no, 1995. Can we have the next page now. Did you know, General -- did our people know that they were involved in a lot of smuggling as far as these medicines are concerned, and other things as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One element was favouring the Muslim side and another one was profiting from these convoys.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that on the 14th of March, 1995, this was approved; namely, that these millions of tablets - if we were to multiply the content of each and every package with the number of packages, it's millions - was all of this approved for entry into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your answer? The interpreters did not hear your answer, Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirmed that I saw the approved list of the quantities of medicine for the enclave. As for this statement of the president about millions, I said that I don't know how many smaller packages are contained in a big package so that we would know the actual number of smaller units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this signed by General Milovanovic on the 12th of March?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there is no signature. It's the signature block, because this is coded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it says here that those who submitted the requests were made aware of the fact that certain quantities had been approved.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can this be admitted now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D2125, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we not admit it in full? Ms. Edgerton, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: They referred to the original for the list which are the names of the medical items, so I do not think we need to have the translation. Would you like to have the translation, though?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Oh, no, I don't think so. I take issue with the mathematical calculations, but that's another story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit it in full.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D05393, please. Just parts of the document, to be as efficient -- or, rather, more efficient. Just two documents that were dated after the directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at this. Do we agree that this was the 27th of March? Again, it was received in the Zvornik Brigade. General Milovanovic is providing information that the movement of convoys has been authorised on the 28th of March with the aim of conducting medical evacuation from Srebrenica in the period between the 20th and 30th of March. And then the third paragraph says this evacuation involves 30 civilian patients of UNHCR and 17 persons accompanying them and then the names are listed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that there is no change in our humanitarian behaviour after directive 7 on the basis of what you've seen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2126, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 65 ter 03643, please. This is the last document from this series.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, do we agree that the then Colonel Miletic is here reporting to the commands of the relevant military districts that authorisation has provided -- has been provided for convoys and then Srebrenica and other places are mentioned. And then under 3 it says delivery of vaccinations for children in Srebrenica and so on. Do you agree that this is the customary behaviour when it comes to humanitarian aid, and we never failed to help children who were ill when it came to these needs. We never withheld such assistance.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this can be seen in the document. It says carry out controls and enable the convoy to pass through unobstructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2127, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have a look at 1D02517.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, General, is it correct that you were engaged at the forward command post in the vicinity of another enclave -- or, rather, so-called protected zone. Let's say the protected zone of Bihac.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is now in English, so I'll just present it to you. It's the 27th of October, 1994. That's the date. Do you agree that this was at the time of a large-scale offensive launched from the Bihac enclave as a result of which you and Milovanovic were sent to that area in order to liberate the Serbian areas that had been occupied?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I do have to point out that this is the 27th of October, and in mid-November I went down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that here General Milovanovic is providing information, it's from the Main Staff, according to which the Muslim forces have set off from the protected zone and they have launched a fierce attack on the Serbian forces with the artillery and infantry? Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that is why one went to the forward command post, and the Main Staff command designated General Milovanovic to be the main commander at that forward command post. The action and the attack of the 5th Corps was in the direction of Krupa to the east and to the south in the direction of Vakuf, over Ripici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is in evidence as Exhibit D710.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just to note, Your Honour, I didn't see a B/C/S translation of this document. So the witness, I note, was agreeing with a question based on the content of the document without being able to read the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, can you clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] President Karadzic asked me about the enclave or the protected zone of Bihac. The date is the 24th of October. That's when the ABiH 5th Corps broke through from the protected zone in the direction of the Krupa settlement and in the direction of Vakuf in the south. I said that that was the reason for which we had been sent to that forward command post. General Milovanovic and a certain number of other officers left immediately, whereas I was ordered by General Miletic to go there. And it was in mid-November that I arrived in the area in Jasenica, and I'm familiar with these events. As for the contents of the document, I haven't read the document because it's in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. So you answered without reading the document. Let's proceed. This is the document you used with General Rose.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 1D054526 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of November, 1994, I believe you're already down there. Have a look at this. It's the forward command post in Jasenica that is concerned here. The date, the 15th of November, and it's a report -- a report to the units of the 2nd command. In the course of our successful counter-offensive at the Krupa-Bihac battle-field, the Muslims have again, true to custom, managed to secure pressure -- well, it's been translated. I won't read through all of it. Does this correspond to the information you had to -- when they attacked, they had success, we wouldn't complain. And when we would get back territory, return territory, they would ask for protection in the so-called falsely demilitarised zones. Does this correspond to the information that you had?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how the events unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2128, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we see 1D05428.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, do you remember that your commander at the time, your immediate commander, appealed to the Muslim 5th Corps to surrender at that place? Have a look at the document. Is that the document in which an appeal is made to them and they're told about how they would be treated. He also says that they are taking into consideration the lives of the civilians, of all the members of the 5th Corps, officers, and so on and so forth, regardless of their rank. It says that their lives will be spared, their families will be able to return and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with all of that. I was down there during this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me just -- how is this relevant? Could you explain this to me, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, even the municipality is not included in the indictment, well, the Prosecution wants to show the context, model of behaviour. This is the model of behaviour for the second -- that man in the army, and his collaborator was General Obradovic. It says the enclaves are full of weapons and the troops are attacking us, and this is just prior to the crisis in Bihac. And we could have entered Bihac if I hadn't signed a truce, but this humanitarian appeal was issued prior to that event. And it also speaks about our relationship to international war law and our respect of that law and other matters for which the indictment has been brought here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We will admit this, and then you have ten minutes to conclude, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2129, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have a look at 1D05429.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While waiting for that document, they did not respond to this appeal, did they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now have a look at this. Four days later, General Milovanovic reports that at the entrance to Bihac, he issues such and such an order. It says in order to break up and destroy the enemy -- I don't have to read it through. We can all see this. He says commence with operations against the enemy force. And at item 2: "Units should follow the previously given axis and tasks whereby I most strictly prohibit the destruction of the town of Bihac. The town must be liberated solely by infantry weapons," and so on and so forth. Have a look at it. I won't read through all of it. And does this correspond to the information you had and does this also correspond to the way in which our army would conduct itself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this intended for the media or does it say "strictly confidential" at the top?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The addresses have been listed. It says the 2nd Corps command, Tactical Group 2, Tactical Group 3, Tactical Group 4, which were integral parts of the 2nd Corps, the Main Staff of the VRS and all the corps, the air force and anti-aircraft defence, for information. So it's an order for these up on the top and for the others it's for their information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it's strictly confidential, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2130.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at 1D5132.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is your old area. The 8th of October, 1995, Colonel Obradovic, and you are speaking with a general from the UN, probably Solje. Who is that? Do you remember this conversation in which you requested that they move, that the Muslim forces move away from the UN, and you said you weren't targeting the UN but you were responding to the Muslim side's action? Do you remember that conversation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not particularly, but I don't really know what the function of this interlocutor of mine is, Solje. If the conversation was intercepted, well, he was probably identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the 2nd Corps of the Muslim army and they said that you told someone from the UN that you weren't targeting them but were responding to action taken. And further down it says it would be good if the Muslim positions weren't close to the UN, and the interlocutor says, Very well, I've understood that. It's the next page in the English version. Were there such cases, they would approach the UN positions and then open fire on us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then we would be accused of clashing with the peace forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the interlocutor says, Very well, I've understood, and you then say good-bye to each other. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was your response not my question when I said that they would accuse us for these clashes with the UN. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you explain again how this is relevant to the case?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I've been indicted for everything here, for sabotage of the UN mandate, amongst other things, the mand -- for sabotage of the mandate of the humanitarian organisations. I've been indicted for obstructing UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is October 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that the relevant period is up until the peace agreement. I think the indictment concerns the period right up to the peace agreement, but the General was in a position to notice that we were falsely accused because of tricks that had been played. The model -- the model, the pattern, that term hasn't been used in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General Obradovic, you confirmed that you were one of the interlocutors in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2131, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we see the last document, 1D5130.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, in 1994, on the 18th of November, at the time you were already down there, the 3rd Corps confiscated some documents from the VRS, and in the part in the box - could we scroll up - it says it has been noticed that the commander of the men -- of the aggressor unit at the time was Colonel Ljubomir Obradovic. And then further down it says from the confiscated documents, one can see that there is one unit formed of members of Muslim nationality, the name of which is Mesa Selimovic. Is that the unit we've been speaking about? And the claim that we would drive out the Muslims regardless of whether they were peaceful or not, is that claim false, and did we move Muslims out of the army? Did we drive them out of the army if they wanted to remain?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give the existence of this unit and what I have already said about Derventa, et cetera, the opposite conclusion can be drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we see the next page. Do we agree that here they are saying that the commander of the Mesa Selimovic company is Nermin Mrdjanovic and a certain Ahmic? Are they both Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but their information is not correct. Mrdjanovic, Nermin, still works in the post office in Derventa, and I don't know Ahmic. I've already mentioned the names of both commanders, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And Nermin Mrdjanovic lived with you throughout that period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's from Dubocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here it says that you issued on the 18th of June, 1992, instructions on how to treat POWs and on how to establish camps for war prisoners. It was signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubomir Obradovic. And there was a supplement to that document on implementation of international war law. This concerned treating prisoners of war and civilians, and it was signed by the deputy commander for morale and so on and so forth. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have camps of any kind, but the second part, that I issued orders, instructions that concerned the treatment of POWs and civilians, well, that is correct. I did write instructions for subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have a look at the next page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we don't have time to further look at this document. We'll mark this document for identification as Exhibit D2143 -- 32, 2132, and it is time for you to put your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General Obradovic, we've only seen each other on two occasions. We didn't really know each other; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber -- are you in a position to tell the Chamber whether you ever noticed that I had an aggressive or intolerant attitude toward our minorities? Was there any information to that effect in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it were not for the next case, the Chamber would be sitting and we could continue, but we should continue next week, but unfortunately we start with Mr. Erdemovic next week or we start with General? I think we can start with the General first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that -- you're talking about the current witness and I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, General Obradovic, and then we'll continue to hear --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't see any reason why we can't proceed that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can finish that on Monday. Yes. General Obradovic, we have to continue, unfortunately, you noticed. My apologies for you to have to stay one more week, but we'll continue on Monday at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, but given that the General is here over a weekend, perhaps he could be cautioned not to speak to anyone about his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I did. General, you know that you are not supposed to discuss about your testimony with anybody else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I think interpreters are -- aha, we have it, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, General, you are not supposed to discuss about your testimony with anybody else. Do you understand that, sir? Please have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of February, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.03 p.m.,
